_schema.title: State Medicaid Enterprise Systems procurement coverage
_schema.scope: State Medicaid enterprise systems and the routes into them. Not general state IT procurement.
_schema.research_method: Web search result snippets only (page fetches were blocked in the build environment). Every fact carries the page it came from and the retrieval date. Fields no snippet supported are null and listed in pending; nothing was inferred. Official state, CMS, eCFR and NASPO ValuePoint pages read as high confidence; vendor announcements, trade press and third-party listings as medium.
_schema.coverage_rule: A query that names a state whose coverage for the requested entity is not_covered returns 409 COVERAGE_GAP with that state's coverage row, never an empty list. partial returns the rows on file with the coverage row beside them.
_schema.top_ten_basis: The ten highest total-Medicaid-spending states in KFF's FY2023 table (order as reported by U.S. News): CA, NY, TX, PA, FL, IL, OH, WA, MA, MI. Total Medicaid spending is a proxy for MES market size, not MES spending itself.

market_context.source: MACPAC issue brief, State Medicaid Enterprise Systems (July 2026)
market_context.use: Sizing context only, never a live feed. Figures are MACPAC's reading of CMS-64 data as quoted in search results.

notes: state_solicitation rows are the RFIs, RFPs and notices found in the research pass, with their status as of the retrieval date. There is no live state portal feed yet; coverage says so for every state.
The CEF numbers equal the paragraph numbers of 42 CFR 433.112(b); the CMS site's table of short names was not read, so short names are MMT's own.
No NASPO ValuePoint portfolio for electronic visit verification, MES data and analytics, eligibility or care management was found.

funding_conditions.name: 75 percent FFP for operations
funding_conditions.requirement: FFP at 75 percent of expenditures for operation of a CMS-approved mechanized claims processing and information retrieval system from the first day of the calendar quarter after the system met the conditions of initial approval. Conditions include meeting 433.112(b)(1) through (22) at the time of approval, continuous operation during the period claimed, beneficiary notices within 45 days of payment of claims, fraud-control-unit access to probable fraud information, and the standards in 433.112(b)(10) through (b)(16).
funding_conditions.vendor_obligation: Operations contracts inherit the conditions; a module that stops meeting them puts the state's 75 percent match at risk.

sources.label: eCFR 42 CFR 433.116

funding_conditions.name: Reduction to 50 percent on disapproval
funding_conditions.requirement: If CMS disapproves a system on reapproval review, FFP for system operations is reduced from 75 percent to 50 percent of expenditures beginning with the first day of the first calendar quarter after CMS issues the written notice.
funding_conditions.vendor_obligation: The financial consequence a state faces when a module falls out of compliance; it shapes how states write performance and remediation terms.

sources.label: eCFR 42 CFR 433.119

funding_conditions.name: Ownership clause in every procurement instrument
funding_conditions.requirement: The state must include a clause in all procurement instruments giving the state or local government all ownership rights in software, modifications and associated documentation designed, developed or installed with FFP; HHS reserves a royalty-free, nonexclusive, irrevocable license for federal government purposes. Commercial off-the-shelf software sold at catalog or market prices to the general public is exempt from the ownership provisions, and FFP is not available for proprietary application software developed specifically for public assistance programs.
funding_conditions.vendor_obligation: Expect the ownership and license clause in every state MES contract; only true COTS at market price keeps its commercial ownership.

sources.label: eCFR 45 CFR 95.617

funding_conditions.name: Streamlined Modular Certification (SMC)
funding_conditions.requirement: SMC replaced MECT and MEET for MES projects initiated after SMD 22-001. After APD approval the state completes the SMC Intake Form with outcomes and CEFs; CMS evaluates the CEF tab at the Operational Readiness Review before go-live and at the Certification Review six to twelve months after go-live, and may periodically review and reapprove systems for the 75 percent match. SHO 25-003 folded EVV into SMC (ending EVV outcomes-based certification) and standardized the APD, MDBT, ORW, alternatives analysis and project-status templates; the templates received PRA approval December 23 2025 and are required from July 1 2026.
funding_conditions.vendor_obligation: A vendor's delivery plan has to land the ORR before go-live and produce the metric data the CR needs; CEFs marked not applicable need an attested justification.
